prediction_pooling: PREDICTION WRITTEN 11:48 PM Pacific 2026-11-20, BEFORE the LSRUN4 results: the 6 % is a pooling bias (Jensen). read_whole's expectation e is the POOLED level of the type's donors (stage_metaa_atlas._col, SEQ_LEVEL pooled), and entropy is concave, so H(pooled level) is higher than the mean of each donor's H; the chain's own expected_H_donors (sorted-cell, 10-31) says so: 'a pooled level (whose entropy is higher than any one donor's)'. A new person therefore reads below 1 in every type: one direction, not depth. It explains all three facts: in-reference reads ~1 (the library is in the pool), held-out against a one-library half reads 1 (no pooling: pass 8, 0.990), never-used against the pooled full atlas reads 0.930 while sorted-cell (donor mode) reads 1.017 on the same libraries. The counted expectation (edit 226) corrects counting noise, not person-to-person spread, so LSRUN4 is predicted to leave whole-sample near 0.93 (within 0.03). The derived fix, nothing fitted: the expected disorder of an unseen person from the atlas's own donor spread: k ~ BetaBinomial(n; mean e, variance sum_k F_k^2 donor_sd_k^2), E[H(k/n)] as in expected_H_counted; predicted to bring whole-sample on the 49 to within 0.03 of 1. Domains (built the same way, -0.047) should move with it; the C-Score (shift +0.001) is built differently and should not.
